title: Normalization after field extension compares by a universal homeomorphism
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $X$ an integral scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $K/k$ be any field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and write $X_K=X	imes_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-base-change]. Let $
u:X^
u	o X$ be its function-field normalization [def-sc-normalization], and let $
u_K:Y	o X_K$ be the componentwise normalization of the reduction of $X_K$ [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. There is a canonical morphism $b:Y	o X^
u	imes_k K$ over $X_K$, induced by the normalization maps. It is a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism].

source.place: Tag 0C3N, label lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields, universal-homeomorphism assertion for arbitrary field extensions, specialized to integral finite-type X.

proof.text: Choose the finite affine cover $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ supplied by the definition of finite type over $k$, omitting empty members. Each $A$ is a finite type $k$-algebra and a domain, since $X$ is integral. Write $A'$ for its integral closure in $F=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, $B_L=A\otimes_k L$, $R_L=(B_L)_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $Q_L=Q(R_L)$. For every extension $L/k$, the generators of $A$ give generators of $B_L$ and $R_L$ over $L$, so $\operatorname{Spec}R_L$ is Noetherian by the finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem. The componentwise affine-chart theorem and the total-fractions product decomposition identify the normalization over $U_L$ with $\operatorname{Spec}B'_L$, where $B'_L$ is the integral closure of $B_L$ in $Q_L$. Indeed the product decomposition identifies $Q_L$ with the product of the fraction fields of the reduced components; integrality in a finite product holds coordinatewise (multiply the finitely many monic annihilating polynomials). Passing from $B_L$ to its reduced quotient changes neither the integral elements in $Q_L$ nor this normalization. Over $U$, the given $X^\nu$ is $\operatorname{Spec}A'$ by its definition.

source.place: Tag 0C3N, label lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields; affine reduction and integral-closure description

proof.text:
The map $F\to Q_K$ given by the fraction-ring lemma sends $A'$ into $B'_K$: a monic equation over $A$ remains a monic equation over $B_K$. Since $B'_K$ is a subring, this gives
$$\varphi_K:A'\otimes_k K\longrightarrow B'_K,\qquad a'\otimes\lambda\longmapsto a'\lambda.$$
On principal opens this construction agrees with restriction: both maps send a fraction to the fraction of its images, and integral closure commutes with localization. The normalizations themselves commute with open restriction. Consequently the local scheme morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi_K$ agree on principal refinements of overlaps and glue to a morphism $b:Y\to X^\nu\times_k K$. Its composites to $X_K$ agree on the affine cover, so it is over $X_K$. This construction, using only the structural ring maps and localization, specifies the canonical comparison without any choice of component enumeration.

source.place: Tag 0C3N, label lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields; canonical comparison and compatibility on affine overlaps

proof.text: Regard $A'\otimes_k K$ as a subalgebra of $F\otimes_k K$: tensoring the inclusion $A'\subseteq F$ is injective because $K$ is flat over the field $k$. The composite into $Q_K$ is the map $\theta_K$ of the fraction-ring lemma restricted to this subalgebra. Since $\ker\theta_K$ consists of nilpotent elements, so does $\ker\varphi_K$ (injectivity of the first map reflects the equation $z^m=0$). This proves the kernel condition even when $A'\otimes_k K$ is nonreduced.

source.place: Tag 0C3N, label lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields; nilpotent kernel of the affine comparison

proof.text: If $K/k$ is separable, apply the separable-normalization comparison to the reduced finite-type scheme $X$. Its single reduced irreducible component is $X$, so its componentwise normalization is $X^\nu$. That comparison identifies the canonical $b$ just constructed with an isomorphism, which is a universal homeomorphism. Hence suppose $K/k$ is not separable. Its characteristic is then a prime $p>0$: in characteristic zero, every finitely generated subextension has a separating transcendence basis by the perfect-field theorem and is therefore separable by the separably-generated-implies-separable theorem, which would make $K/k$ separable by definition.

source.place: Tag 0C3N, label lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields; separable case; reduction to positive characteristic

proof.text: Fix $b\in B'_K$. Represent it as $c/d\in Q_K$ with $c,d\in R_K$ and $d$ a nonzerodivisor, and choose lifts of $c,d$ to $B_K$. Choose a monic equation $b^m+\alpha_1b^{m-1}+\cdots+\alpha_m=0$, with $\alpha_i\in B_K$. Each lift and coefficient is a finite sum of pure tensors. Let $H\subseteq K$ be the field generated over $k$ by their finitely many scalar coefficients. They descend to $B_H$. Their denominator is a nonzerodivisor in $R_H$: an element it annihilates maps to zero in $R_K$, hence is zero by the injectivity of $R_H\to R_K$. Thus $b_H=c_H/d_H$ exists in $Q_H$. Injectivity of $Q_H\to Q_K$ reflects the displayed monic equation, so $b_H$ is integral over $B_H$ and maps to $b$. This is the finite-coefficient descent in the source, with both the denominator and the equation checked.

source.place: Tag 0C3N, label lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields; finite coefficient field for one integral element

proof.text: Choose a finite transcendence basis $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ of $H/k$. Put $T=k(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ and let $E$ be its separable algebraic closure inside the algebraic extension $H/T$. The separable-first theorem gives that $H/E$ is purely inseparable. The same $t_i$ are a transcendence basis of $E/k$, and $E/T$ is separable algebraic. Thus $E/k$ is separably generated and hence separable. For each of the finitely many scalar coefficients in lifts of $c_H,d_H,\alpha_i$ choose a $p$-power taking it into $E$, using the pointwise conclusion of the separable-first theorem. Choose $q=p^n$, $n\ge1$, divisible by all those powers. The Frobenius identity for finite sums shows that $c_H^q,d_H^q$ and every $\alpha_i^q$ belong to the images of $R_E$ or $B_E$, respectively. No uniform exponent for all elements of $H$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0C3N, label lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields; separable-first decomposition and a common exponent for the finite coefficient set

proof.text:
Write $c_H^q=\bar c$, $d_H^q=\bar d$ for the images of elements of $R_E$. The element $\bar d$ is a nonzerodivisor in $R_E$: if $\bar d x=0$, inject into $R_H$, where $d_H^q$ is a nonzerodivisor, and then use injectivity again. Hence $u=\bar c/\bar d$ belongs to $Q_E$ and maps to $b_H^q$. Raising the monic equation of step 5 to the $q$th power gives
$$u^m+\alpha_1^q u^{m-1}+\cdots+\alpha_m^q=0$$
in $Q_E$, because it holds after the injective map $Q_E\to Q_H$. Thus $u\in B'_E$. Apply the existing separable-normalization comparison to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $E/k$: on these affine charts its canonical algebra map $A'\otimes_k E\to B'_E$ is an isomorphism. Choose a preimage of $u$. Its image in $A'\otimes_k K$ maps under $\varphi_K$ to $b^q$, by the tower compatibility in the fraction-ring lemma. This proves that every $b\in B'_K$ has a positive $p$-power in the image of $\varphi_K$.

source.place: Tag 0C3N, label lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields; Frobenius of the equation and application of the separable case

proof.text: Apply the power-generated-spectrum criterion to $\varphi_K$, with the prime $p$ fixed above. Step 3 gives its nil kernel; step 7 shows that every element of its target, hence in particular a set of algebra generators, has a $p^n$-power in its image. The other required element $p^n b$ is zero because the rings have characteristic $p$, and thus also belongs to the image. Therefore $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi_K$ is a universal homeomorphism. These are the restrictions of $b$ to an open cover of its target, from step 2. After any base change to that target the pulled-back opens still cover; on each, the induced continuous map is a homeomorphism. Their inverse maps agree on overlaps by uniqueness of an inverse, so they glue to a continuous inverse. This verifies the defining universal-homeomorphism condition for the global $b$.

source.place: Tag 0C3N, label lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields; Tag 0BRA and gluing the universal-homeomorphism property
